title: CI: shared Rust version pin and cached toolchain
summary: The CI workflow now declares the Rust version once in a workflow-level `RUST_VERSION` env var, and both Rust-consuming jobs install that version instead of a hard-coded literal. Each of those jobs also gains an `actions/cache` step over `~/.rustup`, keyed by OS and the pinned version, so a warm cache lets `rustup toolchain install` short-circuit. The comments record that this is interim: issue #244 will bake the toolchain into the dev container image and move the pin to `rust-toolchain.toml`, at which point the install step disappears.

nodes.label: Push / pull_request
nodes.subtitle: github.ref, github.event
nodes.summary: Repository events that select the workflow and supply the ref used by the concurrency group.

nodes.label: Concurrency group
nodes.subtitle: ci-${{ github.ref }}
nodes.summary: Cancels in-progress runs for the same ref so superseded commits do not keep runners busy.

nodes.label: ci.yml
nodes.subtitle: workflow-level env + job graph
nodes.summary: The workflow file itself. This change adds a top-level `env` block holding `RUST_VERSION: 1.99.0`, which every job can now read, and rewrites the two toolchain install steps to consume it.

nodes.label: RUST_VERSION
nodes.summary: The single source of truth for the Rust version. Previously the literal `1.99.0` was duplicated in two install steps; now it is declared once at workflow scope and interpolated as `${{ env.RUST_VERSION }}`. The comment records that this pin is interim until issue #244 moves it into `rust-toolchain.toml`.

nodes.label: dsh-plugin
nodes.subtitle: plugin checks
nodes.summary: The plugin job. It does not build Rust, so it is untouched by this change and serves as the contrast case for the two jobs that do.

nodes.label: Rust build job
nodes.subtitle: detect → cache → install → build
nodes.summary: The first Rust-consuming job. It gains a `Cache the Rust toolchain` step before the install step, and its install step now reads `${{ env.RUST_VERSION }}` instead of the literal version. The install step is still gated on the `detect` step finding a root `Cargo.toml`.

nodes.label: Rust lint job
nodes.subtitle: fetch-depth 0 → cache → install
nodes.summary: The second Rust-consuming job, which checks out full history and then installs the same toolchain. It receives the identical cache step and the identical `env.RUST_VERSION` substitution, which is what makes the shared pin worth having.

nodes.label: Cache the Rust toolchain
nodes.subtitle: actions/cache@55cc834
nodes.summary: A new step in both Rust jobs. It caches `~/.rustup` under the key `rustup-${{ runner.os }}-${{ env.RUST_VERSION }}` with restore key `rustup-${{ runner.os }}-`, so a cache hit for the exact OS and version restores the installed toolchain and the subsequent `rustup toolchain install` becomes a no-op.

nodes.label: Install the pinned Rust toolchain
nodes.subtitle: rustup toolchain install $RUST_VERSION
nodes.summary: The existing install step, now parameterised. It runs `rustup toolchain install "${{ env.RUST_VERSION }}" --profile minimal --component clippy,rustfmt` followed by `rustup default` on the same value, so the version is no longer written twice in the file.

nodes.label: Cache the build
nodes.subtitle: cargo target cache
nodes.summary: The pre-existing cargo build cache that follows the toolchain install. It is unchanged, but it is the reason the toolchain cache matters: a cold toolchain install delays the point at which the build cache can be used.

nodes.label: Actions cache backend
nodes.subtitle: actions/cache@55cc834
nodes.summary: GitHub's cache service, addressed by the pinned `actions/cache` commit. It stores and restores the `~/.rustup` archive under the version-scoped key.

nodes.label: rustup distribution
nodes.subtitle: static.rust-lang.org
nodes.summary: The upstream channel that serves the toolchain archives. On a cache miss the install step downloads from here; on a hit it is not contacted.

edges.label: ${{ env.RUST_VERSION }}
edges.summary: The connection this change is really about: one workflow-level value now feeds both install steps, so the version can no longer drift between jobs.

edges.label: ${{ env.RUST_VERSION }}
edges.summary: The second consumer of the same pin, in the lint job. Together with the build job this is the duplication the change removes.

flows.title: Provisioning the pinned Rust toolchain
flows.summary: How a Rust job gets its compiler after this change: the cache step tries to restore `~/.rustup` under an OS-and-version key, and the install step either finds the toolchain already present or downloads it from rustup.

messages.label: GET rustup-{os}-{version}
messages.note: A hit restores the whole `~/.rustup` directory, including the installed 1.99.0 toolchain and its clippy and rustfmt components.

messages.label: rustup toolchain install $RUST_VERSION
messages.note: With a warm cache this resolves locally; on a miss it downloads the minimal profile plus clippy and rustfmt.

messages.label: fetch toolchain archive
messages.note: Only reached on a cache miss, which is the case the new cache step exists to avoid.

views.title: CI pipeline and the Rust toolchain path
views.summary: The workflow, its jobs, and the two external services the Rust jobs depend on. The hero edges are the new `RUST_VERSION` pin feeding both install steps.

views.title: Toolchain provisioning sequence
views.summary: The ordered steps a Rust job takes to obtain its compiler, from cache lookup through install to default.

steps.heading: One pin, two jobs
steps.body: `RUST_VERSION` is declared once at workflow scope and read by both install steps.

steps.heading: Cache before install
steps.body: Each Rust job restores `~/.rustup` under an OS-and-version key before installing.

steps.heading: Warm path vs cold path
steps.body: A cache hit makes the install a no-op; a miss falls through to rustup distribution.
